gloss: carrot and stick; reward and punishment

definitions.gloss: carrot and stick; reward and punishment; the soft and hard approach
definitions.explanation: A strategy of using both incentives (rewards) and deterrents (punishment) to achieve a desired outcome. Literally 'candy and whip.' Equivalent to the English expression 'carrot and stick.'

examples.japanese: {飴|あめ}と{鞭|むち}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: To use the carrot and the stick appropriately.

examples.japanese: あの{上司|じょうし}は{飴|あめ}と{鞭|むち}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}がうまい。
examples.english: That boss is good at using the carrot and stick approach.

examples.japanese: {子育|こそだ}てでは{飴|あめ}と{鞭|むち}のバランスが{大切|たいせつ}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: They say the balance between reward and punishment is important in child-rearing.

notes: Literally 'candy and whip.' The expression is thought to derive from Bismarck's domestic policy approach (Zuckerbrot und Peitsche, 'sugar bread and whip'). Common collocations: {飴|あめ}と{鞭|むち}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける (to skillfully alternate between reward and punishment), {飴|あめ}と{鞭|むち}の{政策|せいさく} (carrot-and-stick policy). Used in contexts of management, parenting, education, and politics.
